events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a safety-typed dispute with an explicit threat allegation, so no automatic money ruling is made and the file goes to a person [F3][F4][RD-1 is not the operative clause here; SAFE-1 governs]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped — two messages, both with times [F5] — so nothing here turns on missing evidence.

What happened, as the record shows: at 17:19 the rider asked to be let out mid-ride ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here.") [F3]; one minute later at 17:20 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The rider's complaint characterises this as a threat to lock her in and says she felt unsafe for the whole ride [F1][F2 place the ride at 17:08–17:31, which brackets that exchange]. The driver's only account is a statement written after the trip claiming the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving and that he told her to sit down "for her own safety" [F6] — a claim, not a contemporaneous chat message, and it does not appear in the thread [F5].

Reading these words in context rather than by keyword: the driver's message is conditional and aimed at controlling the rider's movement inside a moving car ("or I lock the doors") and follows a request to be released from the ride. A statement that the doors will be locked if the rider does not comply is capable of being intimidation or abuse of a passenger under Ryde's code of conduct, and the screening rule is asymmetric — a false "suspected" costs a human look, a missed threat that lets an automatic outcome execute does not. I therefore record this as suspected, not confirmed, because intent and tone cannot be fixed from two lines and the driver's safety explanation is unrebutted on the record. Ryde's code of conduct bars abuse of any kind, including threats and intimidation [SAFE-1], and the complaint is precisely that class of allegation. Where a safety incident or dangerous-driving allegation is live, the clause directs escalation rather than an adjudicated outcome [SAFE-2].

I note for the reviewer what I checked and did not decide: the GPS shows the actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km), so there is no measurement basis for a route-deviation refund on these facts [F1] and no off-route segment to review. Neither profile fact decides anything — the rider has no prior disputes and the driver has none upheld in 90 days, and profile facts may never be used alone to find a case made out [F7][F8]. For completeness, the fare side of the file produces nothing refundable: the service is RydeX with a fixed quoted fare of $32.86, and on a non-metered service a distance variance of -0.1 km cannot change the fare at all, so no chargeable add-on item survives to be refunded [F1][RD-2]. Because the safety screen controls and no money is ordered, the amount is left null.

No fare adjustment is proposed.
